title: Fog
description: Looking straight up between the Canary Wharf towers into a summer cumulus sky, with air that knows how far away everything is. Drag up or scroll to shorten the visibility, down to clear it; the haze gathers a little thicker wherever the pointer rests. The far towers go first, turning the blue of the sky they stand in, the cumulus fade behind the veil while their edges stay crisp, and the glass corner overhead stays sharp in front of it all.
intent: Aerial perspective, after Makoto Shinkai's skyward city shots and the worm's-eye summer photographs herb loves: converging towers, a cobalt zenith, cumulus. Beer-Lambert transmittance per pixel and per channel (Rayleigh-leaning, blue extinguished first) through a haze layer that thins with height, along a metric distance converted from a Depth Anything V2 map. Drag sets the meteorological visibility (Koschmieder, beta = 3.912 / V) from 50 km to 150 m, mapped so the visible change runs evenly along the gesture: log V moves fast at the front, past the clear-day kilometres that change little in a 400 m frame, so the far towers are half blue by fog 0.3 (~1.3 km) and cobalt silhouettes with the low sky veiled by 0.5 (~350 m). The extinction is depth-separated: the street around the viewer is swept clearer, the haze's density rising from nothing at the eye to full beyond about 60 m (a ray to d crosses d - d0 ln(1 + d / d0) of it), so the glass corner 30 m off sees a fifth of its straight-line air and keeps its contrast (within about 10% of a clear day at fog 0.5) while the far towers go. That clear pocket closes over the second half of the drag, which is what takes the near towers and the street. The in-scattered light comes from the sky itself. In front of a tower it is the open sky at that tower's own elevation, measured off the plate between the clouds (#5a9fcc low, deepening toward #2f7fb8), with extinction per channel and no lift toward white, so a far tower fades to a cyan-cobalt silhouette that keeps its floor lines, never to milk. In front of the sky it is the broadest level of a normalised blur of the sky pixels only, so no blurred copy of a cloud is printed into the haze, pulled to a clear cyan (#9fc4d6) low in the sky and never lifted past #d6e4e8, so the veil cannot go milky. Distance and sky matte are snapped to the silhouettes (Depth Anything pulls a tower's edge toward the sky's distance for tens of pixels; each edge band takes its tower's interior distance instead), so the haze stops exactly where each tower does; the matte the air reads is coverage, not a switch: along each silhouette a guided filter on the plate's own colour softens the snapped matte onto the plate's edge, and every edge pixel blends the tower's distance and air with the sky's by how much of it is sky, so the silhouettes keep their sub-pixel shape at any size instead of stair-stepping. The sky is seen through a thinner column of the haze than the street, by airmass (1 / cos of the zenith angle, floored at 0.15), so the zenith stays clear and the low sky thickens gradually; and the haze in front of it only veils it, keeping at least 65% of the cumulus' local detail (the plate less its blur at the scale of the cloud's forms) so the low cloud reads as cloud through the air: forward-scatter softening touches the towers, never the clouds. The plate is two Poly Haven HDRIs (CC0, from their 16k captures) rendered at 3840 through the same stereographic rays: canary_wharf for the towers, docklands_01 for the sky, its cumulus unmixed from the capture's own blue, laid back over a radial cobalt (pale #2081AC where the sky meets the towers, #044984 in the middle of the opening) by a feathered cover so the edges thin as they did in the photograph, and split-graded from cyan-grey (#B7C5C5) in the shaded folds through #DFE1DE to #FFF1E2 on the sunlit tops. A film finish runs last: a diffusion bloom, a filmic shoulder whose top end lands the cloud tops near #FFF1E2, glass graded away from the sky's blue, a thin amber halation under the highlight edges (the sunlit cumulus and glints only, never the pale cyan sky against a tower), and 24 fps grain at scan scale held for two frames.
